chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Uzafir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I fast these three days of the month. Sometimes I travel, and sometimes an illness befalls me, so is it obligatory upon me to make them up?' He said to me: 'Only the obligatory [fasts] necessitate making up. As for the non-obligatory [fasts], you have the choice in them.' I said: 'The choice during travel and illness?' He said: 'Illness, Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, has exempted you from it, and travel: if you wish, make it up, and if you do not make it up, there is no blame upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up optional fasts missed during travel or illness in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the strict obligation of making up obligatory fasts and the flexibility granted for voluntary (nafl) fasts, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in supererogatory acts. While illness provides a complete exemption from making up these fasts, travel allows the individual the choice (khayr) to either make them up or leave them without sin, emphasizing that voluntary worship is not a binding debt like obligatory duties. This ruling underscores the theological distinction between fard (obligatory) and nafl (voluntary) in Shia jurisprudence, where the latter carries less weight in terms of accountability if missed.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Amro Bin Usman, from Uzafir who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I tend to Fast these three days during the month. So, sometimes I travel, and sometimes an illness hits me. Does it Obligate the making up for it upon me?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘But rather, the Obligatory (Fasts) necessitate it. But, as for the other than the Obligatory (Fasts), so you are with the choice in it’. I said, ‘With the choice during the journey and the illness?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The illness, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Exempted it from you, and the journey, if you so desire to, so make up for it, and if you don’t make up for it, so there is no blame upon you’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Hilal from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Adhafir who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I fast these three days of the month but perhaps I travel or become ill, am I required to complete its Qada’ (compensatory fast)? He (the Imam) said, ‘Qada’ (compensatory fast) is obligatory for obligatory fast which is missed. In the case of optional fast it is up to you.’ I then asked, ‘Is it up to one’s choice even when on a journey and in illness?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘In the case of illness Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has exempted you, but in the case of journey you can complete its Qada’ (compensatory fast) and if you did not do so it is not harmful.’”
